result_text:
Tickets now carry the support agent they're assigned to, and the agent shows up in every listed query. Nothing is committed.

- **`schema.sql`**: `support_ticket` has a new nullable `agent VARCHAR(100)` column. The repo has no support-agent table, so the agent is stored as a free-text name like "Sam".
- **`model/SupportTicket.java`**: the record has a new last component `agent`. The old 9-argument constructor is kept as an overload that leaves the agent null, so existing callers and tests compile unchanged.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupportTicket` inserts and returns the agent. The nine listed queries (`findSupportTicketByNumber`, the open-by-customer/priority/region/sales-rep/product lists, the with-order list, the old high-priority list, and the open-on-date list) select `agent` and map it. `updateSupportTicketStatus` only touches status and closed date, so the agent is kept.
- **`service/SupportTicketService.java`**: new overload `create(..., LocalDate date, String agent)`. The existing 6-argument `create` delegates with a null agent. `changeStatus` copies the agent into the returned ticket.

I ran the nine ticket-related test classes offline (`SupportTicketTest`, `ClosedTicketsTest`, `TicketsPer*Test`, `RegionReportTest`, `DashboardTest`, `RegionManagerTest`): 28 tests, no failures. I did not add a test that checks an agent round-trips through the lists.

Two things I left alone because the task didn't name them: `listClosedSupportTickets` (the closed-ticket report) doesn't show the agent, and nothing in the UI or demo data passes an agent yet, so the agent is always null in practice until a caller uses the new overload.
